newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria depo rates flat as demand edges up.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria depo rates flat as demand edges up.

text.p: Demand for interbank deposits edged up on Bulgaria's money market on Wednesday due to treasury paper payments, but supply was still high enough to meet it and depo rates were steady from Tuesday, dealers said.
"Bids for short-term deposits slightly increased, probably because today banks have to pay for the government securities they bought on Monday," said a dealer.
Banks bought three- and six-month discount T-bills with a total par of 30 billion levs at Monday's auctions. Settlement for the auctions is made on Wednesday.
Spot week rates stood flat at 2.5-3.0 percent annually and overnight depo rates were also unchanged at 1.50-1.75 percent annually.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 2.01 percent on Tuesday, down from 2.38 percent on Monday, a central bank official said.
The central bank simple annual main interest rate has been set at 5.42 percent since Monday, down from 6.12 percent last week. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom +359-2 91188
